subject.title: Browser tool should reject or redact URLs with embedded credentials instead of passing them through

question: Should browser page navigation reject HTTP(S) URLs with embedded username/password userinfo before any local, proxy, Playwright, Chrome MCP, or Chromium dispatch?
rationale: The guard reduces credential exposure, but it intentionally stops URL-embedded Basic-auth navigation workflows, so the security boundary and compatibility tradeoff need maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Fail Fast And Redact
options.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact surfaced URL text, and point users to authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or browser credentials.

options.title: Redact But Keep Passing Through
options.body: Keep URL-embedded Basic auth working while improving logs/errors, accepting continued browser-runtime pass-through.

options.title: Defer For Browser Auth Design
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers define a broader browser-auth story and decide whether URL userinfo remains supported.

recommendation.title: Fail Fast And Redact
recommendation.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact surfaced URL text, and point users to authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or browser credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin/runtime history and policy-sensitive security boundary point to steipete as the strongest routing owner from the inspected history.
